lines.text: Can a 9 dollar knife sharpener really beat a 900 dollar one?
First he grinds every knife dull on a steel rod until it needs 1800 grams of force to cut.
The tester measures how hard you push to slice a thin strip so the lower the number the sharper the blade.
The 9 dollar Rada brings it back to 230 which already counts as kitchen sharp.
But the 67 dollar Lansky hits 110 which is sharper than the knife was brand new.
And the 900 dollar Wicked Edge hits 100 and shaves the hair right off his arm.
That's only ten grams better than the Lansky so you pay 13 times more for a tiny gain.
beats: ai:a tall stack of dollar bills next to a tiny stack of dollar bills on a workbench

lines.text: Then he takes a butter knife that needs 2000 grams to cut and grinds it on an electric sharpener for 30 minutes.
And it slices paper and hits 160 which is sharper than most new chef's knives.
Because sharpness is just a thin straight edge so even cheap soft steel can get scary sharp for a while.
beats: ai:extreme macro of a razor sharp steel knife edge glowing in light

lines.text: So which sharpener would you buy?
